messages:
kevin: FYI SeleneCorp hit isolation again tonight during a routine peering rollover. seen ~15 minutes of failed head requests, fallthrough to hosted worked but latency spiked.

maria: Ugh. This looks familiar — same hap pattern as last month (route prop + onprem firewall idle).

sasha: Do we have the packet captures / flow logs from the time window? I can correlate with the BGP flaps.

kevin: attaching quick snippet of the LB logs below and an error line from customer healthcheck:
```
2026-03-22T22:14:03Z selene-prod us-east-1 lb1 ERROR conn_reset src=10.12.4.2 dst=172.31.9.44 reason=icmp_frag_needed
2026-03-22T22:14:10Z selene-prod us-east-1 healthcheck FAIL code=504 route=peer-us-east
```

aj: devops-bot pulled the peering events: <peering-event-2791234567> — shows route withdraws at 22:13:58 and 22:14:07, short interval. :eyes:

devops-bot: Incident note: automated fallback to hosted models triggered at 22:14:12. No token loss, but 180s higher p95.

lia: My read: probability high it's MTU/ICMP blackhole on-customer-edge combined with our route flap damping. We saw similar remediation last time but owner was rotated mid-sprint.

maria: Action items proposal (short):
- A1: Confirm onprem firewall is allowing necessary ICMP types (owner: @sasha) due 2026-03-25 EOD
- A2: Add explicit MTU test to Selene onboarding and add automated alert on ICMP unreachable patterns (owner: @lia) due 2026-03-28
- A3: Update peering runbook to include immediate (10m) fallback to dedicated fallback pool rather than full hosted fallback, to preserve SLA (owner: @kevin) due 2026-03-26
- A4: Postmortem follow-up for recurring pattern — assign recurring-pattern POV and monthly cadence (owner: @maria) due 2026-04-02

sasha: I'll grab flow logs and call Selene infra lead tomorrow. I can also verify the firewall rules ourselves if they give temporary access. Marking A1 in my queue.

kevin: For A3 I can make a quick PR to rollout policy. Plan: add a route-policy tag on customer config, default to ded-fallback within 2m. I'll draft today.

lia: For A2 — adding automated alert: I'll surface a new metric `peer.icmp_unreach_count` + a 5m anomalous increase threshold. Will test in staging.

maria: Maria: Let's keep this tight. Two additional items:
- A5: Retro note: rotate ownership process so remediation owners persist across adjacent sprints, capture in oncall runbook (owner: @aj) due 2026-03-30
- A6: Create a small synthetic that reproduces short withdraws to validate fallback behavior (owner: @lia + @kevin) due 2026-04-05

aj: A5 acknowledged. I'll add to runbook and ping product for sprint allocation.

kevin: tagging the customer success contact to prep wording for Selene: "we've opened remediation items and will schedule an infra touchpoint" — @maria do you want to own comms?

maria: Yes, I'll draft and share by EOD tomorrow.

devops-bot: Follow-up checklist created: https://redwood-internal/tasks/SELENE-POST-2791234567 (auto-created items: A1,A2,A3,A4,A5,A6)

kevin: Quick question — is there any chance this is a routing policy on our side? I can confirm kernel args and MTU on the peer interface next window.

sasha: We'll confirm both sides. If customer firewall is blocking ICMP frag/needed then MTU mismatch symptoms appear. Also check for VXLAN fragmentation if they're onprem.

lia: I'll add VXLAN MTU probe to the synthetic.

maria: OK team — please update the task when work starts. We'll reconvene next Tue 09:30 to review progress. If owners hit blockers ping here. :white_check_mark:

kevin: noted, updating A3 PR now.

sasha: Flow logs uploaded to the ticket and shared with Selene contact. Starting A1.

aj: Runbook PR queued.

lia: Alert + synthetic in staging, will notify when ready for canary testing.

kevin: thanks everyone. closing daily check-in for this thread.
